What we do

An unmatched end-to-end joinery service

Contact us
About us

Our purpose

We design, build and install high quality, functional kitchens and joinery solutions on-time and on-budget.

In an industry that is often hit and miss, we look at every project as an opportunity to go further to get things right. Across residential, commercial and design audiences, our process ensures a consistently high level finished result.

Our kitchen and joinery solutions include, but
are not limited to:

Kitchen

Pantry

Laundry

Bathroom

Wardrobe

Storage

Living

Office

Shop Fit-out

Custom

How we do it

We care above all else.

It’s the core of Innokit’s work – we care about hitting the deadline, achieving the best possible finish, owning (and rectifying) any mistakes, keeping to the budget, communicating well and finishing the job with everyone as friends.

Why we do it

We’re driven to deliver.

It’s in our DNA – simply put we love making spaces for our clients that meet their unique needs and are delivered exactly how and when they expected. Our work connects people to places.

A glimpse into our process

1

Concept Design

Clients, architects or designers provide a design.

OR

We develop a concept design based on discussions with the client.

2

Quoting

Once the concept design is finalised, we provide a quote.

Upon approval, a deposit invoice is issued to the client.

3

Drawings

After the deposit is received, we begin the shop drawing process.

This includes:

  • Communication with client
  • Production timeline
  • Shop drawings (up to three revisions)
  • Final approval
4

Site Measure

A site visit is conducted to record precise measurements of the space. This can take place either before, during or after the shop drawing process.

5

Manufacturing

The manufacturing process commences.

This includes:

  • Cutting list is completed.
  • Materials and hardware ordered.
  • Materials are cut on CNC machinery.
  • Painting process (if applicable).
  • Assembly of cabinetry.
  • Dispatch inspection is performed.
6

Delivery

A delivery date is scheduled with client and a progress invoice is issued.

Cabinetry and doors are protected with film before being loading into the delivery trucks.

The joinery items are delivered to their designated locations with care.

7

Installation

Installers utilise detailed shop drawings to complete the installation within the agreed timeframe.

A handover form is signed by the client upon completion.

8

Defects

Any defects noted in the handover form are promptly addressed.

Site visits may be conducted to assess and resolve issues.

Once all defects are rectified, the final invoice is issued.
